//: Only real HTML documents can be audited. This config previously also
collected /manifest.webmanifest, which is served as
application/manifest+json, so Lighthouse aborted that run with
NOT_HTML and failed the entire job.
There is only one HTML document worth auditing: the SPA entry at /.
The PWA share-capture.html is deliberately NOT listed - it reads its
query string and immediately location.replace()s to /?share=<id>, so
auditing it would measure the SPA root a second time. Verified:
requested=/share-capture.html, finalUrl=/?share=<generated-id>.
The manifest is data, not a page. It is validated by the browser when
the PWA is installed; Lighthouse has nothing to audit in a JSON file.
Audit IDs must exist in the Lighthouse version this repo pins
(@lhci/cli 0.14.0 -> Lighthouse 12). An unknown ID is not ignored -
it fails the job with '"<id>" is not a known audit', which is how a
typo or a removed audit becomes a confusing red build.
Two axe-derived IDs that Lighthouse does NOT have were removed:
nested-interactive  -> dropped; see below
region              -> landmark-one-main (already listed)
Do NOT substitute focusable-controls, interactive-element-affordance or
use-landmarks for them. They exist, but all three are
scoreDisplayMode 'manual' - Lighthouse cannot pass or fail them
automatically, so they return no score and asserting on them fails the
job with 'Audit did not produce a value at all'. A manual audit is a
prompt for a human reading the report, not a gate.
The nested-interactive and region rules are still enforced, by the
engine that can actually assert them: `npm run a11y:axe` runs axe-core,
where both are real rules and a violation fails the build. See
tests/helpers/axe.ts and tests/e2e/a11y-axe.spec.ts.
Every remaining ID either returns a score (binary/numeric) or is
notApplicable because the page has no such element. Both are fine for
an 'error' assertion. The only disqualifying mode is 'manual', which
is why none of the three manual audits above are listed.
